title: Ive been using claude code to program the ecosystem and minds of creatures that live in a megadungeon, the results are interesting.
author: Motapocatl
selftext: The way behavior emerged from these new systems results in interesting stuff, the thing that I feel I overlooked the most was the non-uniformity of their behavior, some creatures will display curiosity like here, and herds of prey animals end up being more aggressive that I would typically associate with them, especially when in crowds or cornered. And it's not how video games typically handle combat being a binary state, a lot of things just dont like you getting close to them and will strike out at you. It feels a lot more organic but the way its so outside of expectation makes me think it's wrong for a dungeon crawler and maybe they should be mindless attack monsters with combat ai.

comments.author: sabertoothedhand
comments.body:
Sounds like it's time to reassess the genre of your project?

Since you put so much effort into simulating the creatures I assume you're not just trying to make a simple project. Might I suggest a Trickster God protagonist, who utilizes the ability to mimic animals to interact with these systems towards non-standard goals? Say they either need to sew chaos among the land for personal goals or help the animals as atonement. This would also go along with certain Native American mythologies where the border between man and beast was very thin in times of legend.

replies.author: Motapocatl
replies.body: Thank you for the response! My biggest inspiration for this game mechanically is probably dungeon meshi/delicious in dungeon, an anime/manga about food and the circle of life in a big dungeon, so I do want to keep it as an rpg, but that trickster who interacts with these systems in ways that dont seem to make sense is actually a really really good idea and I think the answer to what I've been wanting to do to distinguish the tlacatecolotl/owl people. before they were just generic monsters and now that they mostly focus on their own needs they've felt like they lacked direction. They are already kinda creepy and I think making them mess with the player will make them more memorable.

replies.author: sabertoothedhand
replies.body:
A fellow of culture! Honestly that was the first thing that came to mind when you described a dungeon ecosystem but it seemed irrelevant to the discussion at the time. 

In that case, are you planning/already implementing a macronutrient system? Distilling a creature into butchered "loot" that each has integer values for macronutrients forms a good baseline for both adding to the dynamic ecosystem (say a creature goes through Iron a lot, the player can deduce its presence from carrion that's missing its liver and a bit of meat) and potentially adding an open-ended cooking system further down the line (grilling loses more fat than frying, sometimes nutrients are destroyed by certain types of cooking, etc). You can also choose to inflict the player with statuses that require excess nutrients of some type, forcing them to hunt/gather outside of their comfort zone. 

Anyway, neat project and together we also eagerly await Ryoko Kui's next work, whenever one gets announced 🤝
